key_insight: Egocentric human video can be a stronger and far more scalable pretraining source for embodied AI than scarce real-robot teleoperation data. The paper argues that human video offers enough embodiment-aligned information to outperform robot-only datasets in pretraining.
problem_solved: Embodied foundation models need large-scale data, but real-robot trajectories are expensive, hard to collect, and limited in diversity. This paper addresses the bottleneck of how to pretrain embodied models with more scalable data without sacrificing useful action and scene understanding.
method: Uses egocentric human video as a large-scale pretraining source for embodied learning.
Compares human video against traditional teleoperated real-robot trajectories for embodied pretraining performance.
Leverages the observation that human first-person footage contains rich interaction, motion, and environment cues relevant to robot learning.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a cheaper and much more scalable path to improving embodied models without relying solely on expensive robot data collection. It could accelerate pretraining pipelines and broaden the diversity of tasks and environments models learn from.

paper_title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
paper_authors: Juncheng Ma, Jianxin Bi, Yufan Deng, Xuanran Zhai, Kewei Zhang
